text: I withdraw the objection. [Connes, III.1, Corollary 7](https://alainconnes.org/wp-content/uploads/book94bigpdf.pdf#page=194) defines cyclic cohomology using cyclically invariant multilinear cochains and the Hochschild coboundary, exactly the Lean construction on its intended complex-algebra domain. The characteristic-two calculation remains correct, but distinguishes this generalized cochain theory from Loday's bicomplex theory; it does not refute Connes' definition. The [published comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/791b4b639b9bfc33c3b9b8cb7b32ce3014bf79f3/TauCeti/RingTheory/CyclicCohomology/Bicomplex.lean#L743) correctly assumes `Algebra ℚ R`, and the module already stated this restriction. No merged declaration-docstring change is present at 791b4b6. This withdrawal is not a new acceptance: the explicit full zero-algebra Check remains unverified.

Confirmed fixed in [the merged documentation correction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/commit/dedf03b072fa86de581d843d6aca1a4726218e4e). The [current statement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/791b4b639b9bfc33c3b9b8cb7b32ce3014bf79f3/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/Regularity/Interior.lean#L774) now uses −∂ᵢ(aⁱʲ∂ⱼu), matching [the actual energy integrand](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/791b4b639b9bfc33c3b9b8cb7b32ce3014bf79f3/TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/EnergyForm/Basic.lean#L79), ∇vᵀA∇u. Lean concludes that the restriction of the H¹ solution to every relatively compact open subset is the first-order part of a W²,² element, exactly interior H² regularity. The theorem and proof are unchanged. The original objection was to the transposed prose, and this correction resolves it. The site still indexes 271e1af4, so its displayed documentation has not yet incorporated the fix.

I withdraw this objection. [The predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Viscosity.lean#L107) packages the two touching-test inequalities; convexity is a separate hypothesis in the substantive Monge–Ampère bridges. The [classical comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/MongeAmpere/Viscosity.lean#L426) explicitly assumes `ConvexOn` and `C²` regularity, and then identifies the predicate with `det D²u = f`. My strictly concave example violates that assumption. Keeping admissibility separate is legitimate generality, not a false theorem. This agrees with the convex elliptic scope of [Amadori–Brandolini–Trombetti, §2](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/39615#page=3). [PR21171](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/21171) clarifies the documentation but remains unmerged; this withdrawal does not depend on it.

The documentation defect is fixed in [ea75fcff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/791b4b639b9bfc33c3b9b8cb7b32ce3014bf79f3/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/Basic.lean#L74). `IsDemushkin` retains the five cohomological/pro-p fields but now explicitly says compactness and total disconnectedness are not parameters. On profinite groups those fields match [Labute, p.106](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/3045C3866BBC24C718D94C18F8F68E58/S0008414X00054158a.pdf/classification-of-demushkin-groups.pdf#page=1); the presentation and finite-generation results separately require the profinite hypotheses. Thus the original ℝ×C₂ example no longer contradicts the documented scope. Published checks cover C₂, ℤₚ², D₀, free-group non-examples, and the rank-one/finite exceptions. The 271 site snapshot still displays the old docstring, so this confirms the source fix without claiming the site has incorporated it.

I withdraw this objection. The declaration asserts that the bundled category with rational Hodge morphisms is abelian; its [coimage–image comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Mixed/CoimageImage.lean#L38) is invertible because rational realization preserves kernels and cokernels and reflects isomorphisms. Allowing infinite carriers does not contradict this claim. The [category definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Mixed/Category.lean#L43) already specifies rational morphisms. This generalizes the finite-dimensional rational setting of [Deligne, §2.3.8](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1971__40__5_0.pdf); it does not identify Deligne’s integral category as a full subcategory, since those morphisms must preserve lattices. The proposed documentation clarification is still unmerged; no source fix is claimed.

Confirmed fixed in [the merged documentation correction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/commit/dedf03b072fa86de581d843d6aca1a4726218e4e). Lean tests the weak equation with ψ²u and gives precisely ∫ψ²|∇u|² ≤ (2Λ/λ)²∫|∇ψ|²u² + (2/λ)∫ψ²fu. The theorem and proof are unchanged. The original objection was to the transposed prose, and this correction resolves it. The site still indexes 271e1af4, so its displayed documentation has not yet incorporated the fix.

The scope correction is valid. The [updated docstring](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/791b4b639b9bfc33c3b9b8cb7b32ce3014bf79f3/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/Hecke.lean#L59) identifies `Tₙ` as the single-double-coset operator `heckeTCuspNat`, distinguishing it from classical composite-index `Tₙ`. Its adjoint is the adjugate double coset, which equals the inverse diamond times the original operator; this is the mechanism of [Diamond–Shurman, Proposition5.5.2](https://cjhb.site/Files.php/Books/Book%20Series/GTM/228%20Diamond%20Shurman%20-%20a%20first%20course%20in%20modular%20forms%20%28GTM%20228%20Springer%29.pdf). The p² scalar-coset discrepancy identified earlier still exists, but no longer contradicts the stated theorem. The inverse diamond, coprimality, positive index and level are correct; T₁ and the character-space specialization are proved. This is fixed on main by cae70278, while the 271 site snapshot retains the old wording.

The documentation issue remains at the site commit and at `791b4b6`. The Lean definition is the infimum of coupling-wise `eLpNorm`s, but [Mathlib’s measurability test](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92) is `AEStronglyMeasurable` relative to each coupling. Failure of global joint measurability therefore does not make every objective infinite. For a non-Borel partition of ℝ with distance 0 within parts and 1 across parts, the distance is not jointly measurable, yet [the Dirac theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L496) gives `W∞(δa,δb)=1` for atoms in different parts. The sentence should refer to failure of coupling-relative almost-everywhere strong measurability.

I withdraw this problem review: it identified an error in the roadmap’s A₂ example, not in the [Lean theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Reflection/Uniqueness.lean#L208). The theorem correctly says that pointwise finite-dimensional indecomposables with equal dimension vectors are isomorphic when the Tits form is positive definite and a sink-admissible ordering is supplied. Its [native A₂ checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Kronecker/Reflection.lean#L215) give `(1,1)→(1,0)`, `(1,0)→(1,1)`, and kill the sink simple. No theorem fix was needed. The [roadmap’s contrary expected images](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/e98875dbbea872d0496e323bc880e2b7fd00beb9/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md#L426) remain a separate specification issue; I do not claim that literal Check has passed.

I withdraw this problem review. The [Lean theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/Freudenthal.lean#L385) states the division-free multiplicity identity for every linear form μ; its docstring already distinguishes the extra hypothesis needed for downward division. [The separate separation theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/Separation.lean#L304) requires `genWeightSpace M μ ≠ ⊥` and `μ ≠ λ`, matching [Humphreys §22.3](https://djvu.online/file/Xw7ovfkTWqu21). The example `λ=0, μ=−2ρ` refutes only the announcement’s unrestricted nonvanishing claim; the identity correctly gives `0=0`. No source fix was needed. The prescribed sl₂/sl₃ recursion checks remain unverified, so withdrawal does not claim those acceptance checks now pass.

Lean gives exactly one H¹₀ element satisfying every weak test identity for each L² forcing, under bounded energy coefficients and coercivity. The theorem and proof are unchanged. The original objection was to the transposed prose, and this correction resolves it. The site still indexes 271e1af4, so its displayed documentation has not yet incorporated the fix.

I withdraw the zero-kernel objection. [The construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Gluing.lean#L103) extends a plan by a kernel and reassociates the product coordinates, exactly the conditional-product construction in [Villani’s gluing lemma](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=25). The [first-marginal theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/271e1af4dd54c50b9192cf3e213b7686843a0b3a/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Gluing.lean#L138) explicitly assumes an s-finite plan and a Markov kernel; the zero kernel lies outside that hypothesis. Defining the operation more generally is legitimate. [PR21170](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/21170) clarifies the prose but is still unmerged. I am not adding an acceptance: the roadmap’s finite-matrix/measure-gluing agreement check remains unverified; the existing finite PMF marginal tests alone do not establish that equality.

Confirmed fixed in [the merged documentation correction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/commit/dedf03b072fa86de581d843d6aca1a4726218e4e). Lean bounds u on the half ball by k + D R^(−n/2) times the L² norm of (u−k)⁺, with D chosen before the domain, solution, level and ball. The theorem and proof are unchanged. The original objection was to the transposed prose, and this correction resolves it. The site still indexes 271e1af4, so its displayed documentation has not yet incorporated the fix.
